😍Morocco like Pinterest: the most beautiful hotels  🇲🇦  📍 Royal Mansour Marrakech One of the most luxurious hotels in the world, where every guest stays in a private riad with its own courtyard and pool. Carved ceilings, mosaics, and palm gardens. Breakfasts on the terrace and a spa under a glass dome. 📍 El Fenn A place where Morocco meets contemporary art. Bright walls, terracotta rooftop pools, vintage furniture, and rich colors. A bohemian vibe with sunsets overlooking the medina. 📍 La Mamounia A true Marrakech legend. Expansive gardens, arched galleries, emerald tiles, and a pool you’ll want to spend all day in. Classic luxury with history. 📍 Riad Yasmine The iconic Instagram riad with an emerald pool and pink walls. Small, cozy, and incredibly photogenic. Breakfast by the pool with flower petals. 📍 Amanjena Minimalism with Moroccan architecture. Sandy tones, reflective pools, and perfect symmetry. 📍 Kasbah Tamadot A hotel in the Atlas Mountains with views over the valleys. Terraces, Berber style, and warm sunset light. 📍 The Oberoi Marrakech Modern luxury with an oriental touch. Grand pools, arches, reflective water, and clean geometry. 📍 Scarabeo Camp White tents in the Agafay desert. Minimalism, sand dunes, camels, and caramel-colored sunsets. #moroccotravel #luxuryhotels #riadlife #travelinspo #bucketlist

Four days in Marrakech, Morocco and I already can't wait to go back! 🇲🇦✨ If you’re planning your first trip to Morocco, Marrakech is the perfect place to dive into the country’s rich culture, incredible food, and beautiful architecture. Between getting lost in the medina, learning to cook traditional Moroccan dishes, and enjoying a little luxury in the Agafay Desert, we packed SO much into four days! One thing I loved most about Marrakech was how every day felt completely different. You can spend one morning exploring centuries of history and the next relaxing poolside with views of the Atlas Mountains. And the hospitality? Some of the best I’ve experienced. 🥹 My biggest recommendation is to leave some room in your Marrakech itinerary to wander, shop, and enjoy the city without rushing from one attraction to the next. 📌 Save this 4-day Marrakech itinerary for your Morocco vacation, and tell me: Would you rather spend a day exploring the souks or relaxing in the Agafay Desert? #MarrakechMorocco #MarrakechItinerary #MoroccoTravel #VisitMarrakech #blacktravelblogger things to do in Marrakech, Marrakech itinerary

🇲🇦😍 Marrakech: uma das cidades mais exóticas e fascinantes do Marrocos! Imagine ruas labirínticas, palácios ornamentados, mercados coloridos, jardins exuberantes e uma arquitetura que parece saída de outro tempo. Marrakech é uma explosão de cores, aromas, sabores e cultura no coração do Marrocos! ✨ 📍 O que conhecer em Marrakech: 🕌 Mesquita Koutoubia – um dos cartões-postais mais famosos da cidade. 🏰 Bahia Palace – um palácio magnífico com jardins e detalhes arquitetônicos impressionantes. 🌸 Jardin Majorelle – um jardim famoso pelo azul intenso e pela vegetação exuberante. 🛍️ Medina de Marrakech – um labirinto de ruas, lojas e mercados tradicionais. 🧡 Jemaa el-Fna – a praça mais famosa da cidade, cheia de movimento e cultura. 🏛️ Ben Youssef Madrasa – uma antiga escola islâmica com arquitetura deslumbrante. 🚪 Bab Agnaou – um dos portões históricos mais impressionantes da cidade. 🌴 El Badi Palace – as ruínas de um antigo palácio de proporções grandiosas. 🧖 Hammam tradicional – uma experiência cultural de banho e relaxamento marroquino. Marrakech é um destino que desperta todos os sentidos e mostra um lado completamente diferente do mundo. 5 things to know before going to Morocco👇🇲🇦 1️⃣ Always carry cash. Morocco is still very cash-based, especially in local shops, markets and smaller restaurants. 💵 2️⃣ Be a responsible tourist. Think twice before paying for animal encounters in Marrakech, particularly the monkeys and snakes in Jemaa el-Fnaa. 🐒 3️⃣ Explore beyond Marrakech. Some of Morocco’s best experiences are outside the city, so make time for places like Chefchaouen, Volubilis and the Atlas Mountains. 🏜️ 4️⃣ Having mobile data when you land makes your arrival so much easier. I use Unpack for my travels. Download the app and use code "ALEX" for 20% off your first eSIM plan. (Link in bio)📱 5️⃣ If you’re visiting on a Friday, make sure you try traditional Moroccan couscous. Une mosquée bâtie sur l'océan. Oui, ça existe, et c'est à Casablanca. 🌊 Tout commence en 1980. Le roi Hassan II annonce un projet fou : doter Casablanca d'un monument à la hauteur de sa taille, la plus grande ville du pays. À l'époque, la ville s'est développée très vite depuis le protectorat français, mais elle n'a aucun édifice religieux majeur. Le roi a une exigence : la mosquée doit être au-dessus de l'eau. Il s'inspire d'un verset du Coran qui dit que le trône de Dieu était sur l'eau. 📖 L'architecte français Michel Pinseau dessine les plans, et le chantier démarre en 1986. Mais construire sur l'Atlantique, c'est un enfer : houle, tempêtes, sel qui ronge le béton et le métal. Il faut des fondations ancrées dans la roche, sous la mer, et des matériaux capables de résister à l'humidité pendant des siècles. Pendant 6 ans, des milliers d'ouvriers et d'artisans marocains travaillent sans relâche : zelliges, bois de cèdre sculpté, plâtre ciselé à la main. ✨ Et pour financer le projet ? Une grande souscription populaire : des Marocains de tout le pays ont donné pour participer. 🇲🇦 En 1993, la mosquée est inaugurée. Résultat : un minaret d'environ 200 mètres, 25 000 fidèles à l'intérieur, 80 000 avec l'esplanade, un toit qui s'ouvre, et un sol en verre pour prier au-dessus des vagues. 🤯 Aujourd'hui, c'est l'un des monuments les plus visités du Maroc. Et c'est l'une des rares mosquées au monde que l'on peut visiter à l'intérieur. #Morocco #MoroccoTravel #Casablancamaroc #Culture #Patrimoine
